content.text: {"what_it_is": {"claims": [{"text": "F-15EX (budget line F015EX) is a U.S. Air Force aircraft procurement line funded in the Aircraft Procurement, Air Force appropriation.", "citation": {"fact_id": "c05ad3ce0481b0ef"}}, {"text": "The F-15EX is a new multirole-capable fighter jet based on the two-seat F-15QA (Qatar) configuration, upgraded with advanced capabilities including the Eagle Passive Active Warning Survivability System (EPAWSS) and USAF F-15 Continuous Delivery and Integration Operational Flight Program software.", "citation": {"fact_id": "e7d5bcfb4a30f458"}}, {"text": "The F-15EX will be used predominantly in defensive and offensive counter-air missions at both Air National Guard and Air Combat Command operational squadrons, and it will perform the Homeland Defense mission while giving combatant commanders strike packages capable of operating in highly contested environments.", "citation": {"fact_id": "e7d5bcfb4a30f458"}}, {"text": "The line covers both new-aircraft advanced procurement and a separate F-15EX Modification effort that retrofits the first 20 in-service aircraft (Lots 1 and 2) to a common production configuration, including installation of upgraded radios, anti-jam GPS, and data-link hardware.", "citation": {"fact_id": "cb4796e48126e4a7"}}, {"text": "F-15EX aircraft have been procured over six lots from FY 2020 (Lot 1) through FY 2025 (Lot 6), and the FY 2026 modification funding also provides 18 sets of Conformal Fuel Tanks and associated hardware to support one operational squadron.", "citation": {"fact_id": "033016199ca94aa7"}}]}, "why_it_matters": {"claims": [{"text": "The program's total funding rises to $3,014,394 thousand (about $3.0 billion) requested for FY 2026.", "citation": {"fact_id": "62f7dc46f85af43f"}}, {"text": "In FY 2024 the program recorded actual spending of $2,739,061 thousand (about $2.74 billion), so the FY 2026 request is a modest increase over recent execution.", "citation": {"fact_id": "ef9a591106ec3c2c"}}, {"text": "The largest single piece of the FY 2026 request is a $2,480,818 thousand (about $2.48 billion) reconciliation (mandatory) request on the P-1 aircraft line.", "citation": {"fact_id": "e8057e2c5f1484ef"}}, {"text": "For the new-aircraft advanced-procurement effort, the FY 2026 request is entirely mandatory: $0 of discretionary and $2,408,818 thousand of reconciliation funding, which pays for aircraft advanced procurement, 21 F-15EX Lot 7 aircraft with conformal fuel tanks, initial spares, and other supporting requirements.", "citation": {"fact_id": "da8fcf0561c0e6e8"}}, {"text": "The F-15EX Modification effort carries a further $286,700 thousand (about $287 million) FY 2026 reconciliation request, all mandatory, for conformal fuel tanks, aircraft modifications, and other supporting requirements.", "citation": {"fact_id": "5768200ce4fbc494"}}, {"text": "The mandatory funds are tied to Section 20007 (Air Superiority) of the Reconciliation Exhibit, and the Air Force awarded the Lot 5 contract and the Lot 6 contract (awarded 22 January 2025) as it built up the fielded fleet.", "citation": {"fact_id": "da8fcf0561c0e6e8"}}]}, "players": {"claims": [{"text": "The program is run by the U.S. Air Force, with funding drawn from the Aircraft Procurement, Air Force appropriation.", "citation": {"fact_id": "92835a9645aa3793"}}, {"text": "The new-aircraft effort's research, development, and integration funding is carried in a separate program element, PE 0207146F, and does not include the eight Lot 1 aircraft funded outside this exhibit in FY 2020.", "citation": {"fact_id": "e7d5bcfb4a30f458"}}, {"text": "In accordance with Section 1815 of the FY 2008 National Defense Authorization Act (P.L. 110-181), the F-15EX is designated as necessary for use by the active and reserve components for homeland defense missions, domestic emergency responses, and military support to civil authorities.", "citation": {"fact_id": "e7d5bcfb4a30f458"}}]}, "recent_developments": {"claims": []}}
